name: What special issues should I expect when adding onto an older Los Angeles home?

mainEntity.name: What special issues should I expect when adding onto an older Los Angeles home?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Older LA homes often come with outdated wiring, plumbing, and unreinforced structures that don’t meet current seismic standards. Tying new construction into old systems frequently reveals hidden problems.

You may need to bring certain parts of the existing home up to code as they’re affected by the addition. This can increase cost but improves safety and reliability.

Key factors:
- Knob‑and‑tube wiring, galvanized plumbing, or undersized panels
- Lack of proper shear walls, anchor bolts, or foundation reinforcement
- Possible termite damage, dry rot, or historic settlement
- Asbestos or lead‑based materials that require special handling

Discuss your home’s age and any known issues openly with your contractor. Plan for exploratory work early in the project so surprises are uncovered and addressed in a controlled way rather than derailing the schedule later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Expect more surprises. Older Los Angeles homes often have outdated wiring, plumbing, and seismic weaknesses, plus possible termite or rot damage. Connecting a new addition can trigger required upgrades to affected areas. Budget extra for investigation and code improvements that make the whole house safer and more reliable.
